defaults.threshold: This is a measured sum of 10 tested phthalates, not a health-based limit or a universal safety rating. Individual chemicals differ in toxicity. No present-day legal-compliance determination or product-specific health prediction is made.
defaults.serving: Per serving used by CR; serving gram/mL amounts were not established from the displayed results table. Do not compare these numbers as equal-size portions.
caveats: Historical sample results, not measurements of current stock, every lot or later formulations.
CR analyzed two or three samples of each food. Lot identifiers, full laboratory reports, analyte-specific concentrations and detection limits were not established in this review.
Totals cover BBP, DBP, DiBP, DCHP, DEP, DEHP, DnHP, DMP, DiNP and DNOP only. The separately tested bisphenols and phthalate substitutes are not included. These are not microplastic particle counts.
Packaging is the description in CR’s corrected table, not proof the packaging caused the measured contamination.
Browse-only: UPC, exact package, serving and lot identity were not verified. Automatic scan matching is disabled.
Detection alone does not establish that eating this product causes harm; these totals cannot by themselves establish safety.
defaults.ties: Consumer Reports published and conducted this investigation and advocates reducing plasticizer exposure. Laboratory identity, project-specific funding and full conflicts were not established from the article; no independent funding audit was performed.
defaults.response: See the updated article for manufacturer responses. General Mills and Gerber emphasized compliance with existing regulations; Gerber also described supplier certifications. Fairlife did not respond to CR. These statements do not independently verify current levels, and no response is inferred for other companies.
